source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Key reproductive figures for sows and gilts: minimum breeding age is 8–10 months, at 70–80% of the sow's final mature weight. A heat period lasts 2–3 days; gilts are best mated on the first day of heat and sows on the second day. Mate twice, 12–14 hours apart. The period between heats is 18–24 days (typically 21). After weaning, a sow should come back into heat within 6–10 days if managed well. Gestation length is 114 days (commonly remembered as '3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days'). If the days between weaning and mating stretch beyond 10 for many sows, the farm is less likely to stay profitable.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
